title: Keyset Pagination Instead of OFFSET
description: Page through a large table in constant time instead of degrading as the page number grows.

data.text: An API pages through a 40-million-row events table with `ORDER BY EventDate DESC OFFSET @n ROWS FETCH NEXT 25 ROWS ONLY`. Page 1 is fast but page 20,000 takes seconds, and rows can be skipped or duplicated when new events arrive mid-browse. Rewrite the pagination.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
-- OFFSET pagination: the engine must find and discard @n rows on every request.
-- Cost grows linearly with the page number.
SELECT EventId, EventDate, Payload
FROM Events
ORDER BY EventDate DESC, EventId DESC
OFFSET 500000 ROWS FETCH NEXT 25 ROWS ONLY;

-- Keyset (seek) pagination: remember the last row you returned, then seek.
-- Constant cost regardless of depth, and stable while new rows arrive.
DECLARE @LastEventDate datetime2 = '2024-06-01T12:00:00';
DECLARE @LastEventId    bigint    = 987654321;

SELECT TOP (25) EventId, EventDate, Payload
FROM Events
WHERE EventDate < @LastEventDate
   OR (EventDate = @LastEventDate AND EventId < @LastEventId)   -- tiebreaker
ORDER BY EventDate DESC, EventId DESC;

-- Index that makes the seek O(log n)
CREATE INDEX IX_Events_Date_Id ON Events (EventDate DESC, EventId DESC)
    INCLUDE (Payload);

data.title: Explanation
data.text: `OFFSET 500000` does not skip cheaply — SQL Server still has to locate and count past those 500,000 rows, so cost grows with depth. Keyset pagination instead asks for rows **after a known position**, which an index satisfies as a single seek: the cost is the same on page 1 and page 20,000. Two conditions make it work: the `ORDER BY` must be backed by a matching index, and it must include a **unique tiebreaker** (`EventId` here) or rows with identical timestamps can be skipped or repeated across page boundaries. The trade-off is that the client cannot jump to "page 47" — it receives a cursor instead. That is a good trade for infinite scroll; for random page access, keep `OFFSET` but cap how deep users can go.
